result.title: GridDriver: On-Board BEV-Based Language Planning and Reasoning
result.summary: Bird's-Eye-View (BEV)-conditioned large language models (LLMs) enable language-interactive driving, but onboard deployment requires efficient perception and continuous planning alongside autoregressive language generation. We present GridDriver, an efficient BEV-conditioned LLM framework combining trajectory prediction, structured driving indicators, natural-language navigation, driving explanations, and scene question answering. Lightweight spatio-temporal BEV perception and spatially structured tokens provide scene context to a shared LLM, while frame-wise scheduling interleaves trajectory prediction with asynchronous language generation. GridDriver achieves competitive performance on public benchmarks, reaching 87.9% PDMS on NAVSIM and 57.6% accuracy on nuScenes-QA with a shared planning and QA checkpoint. Spatial representation analyses demonstrate improved geometric information retention and trajectory prediction compared with Q-Former compression. The system achieves 32.7 ms standalone planning latency and 9.4 plans/s in an onboard ROS 2 pipeline. We further evaluate planning on our own data recordings and demonstrate open-loop onboard operation on a research vehicle. Across public benchmarks and real-world evaluations, we identify strengths and limitations of the BEV-based approach.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 GridDriver，以轻量时空 BEV 感知和空间结构化 token 为共享 LLM 提供场景上下文，并用帧级调度交错轨迹预测与异步语言生成，实现车载语言交互驾驶。
AI.relevance_reason: 其对 BEV 空间表示与 Q-Former 压缩的几何信息保留对比分析，可能为 LVR 中视觉细节是否留存于内部状态提供可核查线索；帧级调度解耦规划与 AR 生成亦可供参考，但主体为驾驶应用，联系较间接。
